interactions.summary: A stray fragment appears before the interview proper and does not clearly belong to either speaker in the main exchange.

Greg frames Jiang as an analyst of power rather than benevolent-governance mythology, introduces Predictive History as a rapidly rising project, and asks why Jiang's history lectures are resonating so strongly.
Jiang begins with the synchronicity story of how the interview came together and treats the meeting as a timely convergence rather than random booking.

He then directly answers the resonance question: history is usually entertaining but incoherent, so he is trying to build a movement that turns historical assumptions about values and mores into predictive models of where societies are going.

speaker_notes.note: The opening fragment appears to be leftover audio from an ad, intro clip, or prior segment rather than part of the interview exchange.

claims.claim: Greg frames conventional geopolitical analysis as weak on true power because it assumes benevolent governance instead of domination, extraction, and hidden motivations.
Greg says Jiang's recent popularity comes from his willingness to explain how power, empire, and historical cycles actually work rather than treating history as neutral chronology.
Jiang says he is trying to start a movement that re-examines how history is analyzed and presented.
Jiang argues that ordinary history teaching often tells entertaining stories but leaves events in disconnected silos, so people fail to see a coherent civilizational narrative.
Each historical story embeds assumptions about values and mores, and those assumptions can be extrapolated forward into the future.
Jiang's core method is that an analytical model of history becomes a predictive model, and future predictions can test whether the historical understanding is actually right.

signature_moments.moment: Greg's opening challenge is that the elite may be incompetent, apathetic, or psychopathic, but the functional result is the same for ordinary people.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sets the interview's anti-naive frame: outcomes matter more than charitable intent when judging power.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang interprets the interview setup itself as a synchronistic event the universe wanted to happen.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the universe wants us to be here today
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It establishes the rapport and slightly mystical tone that lets the conversation move beyond ordinary policy commentary.

signature_moments.moment: History becomes predictive when you realize every story already smuggles a model of human values and behavior into the future.
signature_moments.source_phrase: your analytical model becomes your predictive model
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the compact methodological kernel of Predictive History and likely the sentence later reads must preserve.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's project of connecting past, present, and future by turning historical interpretation into testable prediction.
A historical explanation built from assumptions about values and social behavior that can be extended forward.
The underlying values and social norms Jiang says are embedded in every historical narrative.

chronology_notes.note: Greg dates Jiang's public rise to lectures posted in April 2024 and says the major viral surge happened in the months leading up to this 2025-10-07 interview.
